newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails vote on new U.N. leader.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails vote on new U.N. leader.

text.p: President Clinton on Friday hailed the selection of a new U.N. secretary-general and defended his decision to deny Boutros Boutros-Ghali a second term as the "right thing to do" to bring about needed reforms.
The U.N. Security Council late on Friday made official its selection of Kofi Annan of Ghana as the next U.N. secretary-general. The 185-nation General Assembly formally will appoint Annan on Tuesday.
"I'm delighted by today's vote," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House after the vote.
He called Annan, 58, who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations, "an able and energetic manager -- professional, impartial, well-versed in the issues at hand, and a true proponent of reform."
Clinton defended his controversial decision to deny Boutros-Ghali a second five-year term as secretary-general by vetoing his election last month.
Saying their was a need for "far-reaching U.N. reform," Clinton said he believed "the United Nations must have a leader who is committed to these goals."
"That is why I decided we needed a new secretary general," Clinton said. "I knew this would be a controversial decision, but it was the right thing to do."

He praised Boutros-Ghali as "an honourable man who has led a great career" but said "we must prepare the United Nations for the demands of the next 50 years. I am confident Kofi Annan will rise to this task with conviction."
Clinton also pledged "to work closely with the Congress to meet America's obligations to the United Nations and to make good on our arrears."

The United States is estimated to owe about $1.3 billion to the United Nations by the end of the year. Part of the delay in paying the U.S. debt rests with opposition in the Republican-controlled Congress to committing funds without reforms to end wasteful spending.

Earlier, Clinton announced that he intended to nominate Representative Bill Richardson, a New Mexico Democrat, to serve as his new ambassador to the world body -- replacing Madeleine Albright, who he has named as secretary of state in his second term.
Clinton said he believed Richardson "will work effectively with the new secretary general to renew and revitalise this historic organisation to take on the challenges of the future."
